title: College Packing Checklist
metaDescription: A complete college packing checklist for dorm move-in: bedding, storage, study gear, kitchen basics, and toiletries. Free, or tailor it with AI in Gisti.
cardDesc: Dorm move-in essentials — bedding, storage, study gear, kitchen basics, and documents.
intro: Packing for college is a balancing act — bring enough to feel at home in a small dorm room, but not so much it won't fit. This college packing checklist covers the essentials students actually use, from twin XL bedding to a power strip and a basic first-aid kit, and flags what to check with your roommate before doubling up. See more study and school checklists.

items.text: Twin XL sheets, a mattress topper, pillows, and a comforter
items.note: Most dorm beds are twin XL, not standard twin — check first.

items.text: Mattress protector and an extra set of sheets
Bath towels, a hand towel, and a quick-dry shower towel
Shower caddy and flip-flops for shared bathrooms
items.note: Flip-flops are non-negotiable in communal showers.

items.text: Toiletries, a toothbrush holder, and a refillable water bottle
Laptop, charger, and a padded sleeve or bag
Power strip with surge protection and a couple of extension cords
items.note: Dorm outlets are always too few and too far away.

items.text: Phone charger, headphones, and any adapters you need
Desk lamp and a small clip-on reading light
Notebooks, pens, highlighters, sticky notes, and a planner
Backpack for class and a reusable water bottle
Under-bed storage bins and a few drawer organizers
items.note: Vertical and under-bed space is where dorms hide extra room.

items.text: Laundry hamper, detergent pods, and a roll of quarters or a laundry card
Basic first-aid kit and any daily medications
items.note: Include pain relievers, bandages, and a thermometer.

items.text: Mini fridge or microwave — coordinate so you and your roommate don't both bring one
items.note: Message your roommate before move-in day.

items.text: A few mugs, plates, utensils, and a reusable food container
Command hooks, poster strips, and a small toolkit
items.note: Adhesive hooks save your deposit — no nails in dorm walls.

items.text: Fan, plus a warm blanket or throw for cold nights
Important documents: ID, insurance card, and a copy of your housing and class schedule
A little decor — photos, string lights, or a rug to make the room yours

faq.q: What size sheets do I need for a dorm bed?
faq.a: Most college dorm beds use a twin XL mattress, which is longer than a standard twin. Buy twin XL sheets and a twin XL mattress topper, and confirm the size with your housing office before you shop, since a small number of dorms use standard twin or full beds.

faq.q: What should I not bring to college?
faq.a: Skip candles, halogen lamps, and most hot plates or space heaters — they usually break fire-safety rules. Don't double up on big items like a fridge, microwave, or TV; coordinate with your roommate first. And leave anything you rarely use at home, since dorm rooms are small and storage is tight.

faq.q: What is the most forgotten item when packing for college?
faq.a: The commonly forgotten ones are a surge-protected power strip, shower flip-flops, a basic first-aid kit, and spare phone and laptop chargers. A small toolkit, command hooks, and a mattress topper are also easy to overlook but make dorm life much more comfortable.
